items.title: cfnrain
items.text:
cfnrain is a command line tool for AWS CloudFormation templates and stacks. It deploys stacks through change sets, packages local files into templates, formats templates, and shows stack logs.

cfnrain is a community fork of AWS CloudFormation Rain. AWS archived Rain on 2026-07-29 and plans no more releases. cfnrain continues from Rain's last commit, which is Rain v1.24.4 plus 22 commits.

Not an AWS project

cfnrain is not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon Web Services.

items.title: What cfnrain does
items.text:
• Deploys stacks with change sets. cfnrain deploy packages the template, asks for parameter values, shows the change set, and waits for your confirmation. Then it streams the progress and prints a summary with any failure messages.
  • Packages local files into templates. Template directives such as !Rain::Embed and !Rain::S3 put file contents or S3 locations into a template. Modules split one template into many files.
  • Formats templates. cfnrain fmt writes templates in one consistent style, keeps your comments, and converts between JSON and YAML.
  • Shows stack logs. cfnrain logs shows the events of a stack and its nested stacks, and hides the events that are not interesting.

items.title: Compatibility with Rain
items.text:
cfnrain works as a replacement for Rain v1.24.4. Your templates, config files and AWS accounts work with no changes:

  • The !Rain::* directives, the Rain: template section, the Modules, Packages and Constants sections, and the bucket Metadata.Rain commands work as before.
  • The RAIN_VAR_* and RAIN_DEFAULT_TAG_* environment variables work as before.
  • cfnrain uses the same artifact bucket (rain-artifacts-<account>-<region>) and the same rain-bucket SSM parameter.
  • Scripts that call rain keep working when you link the name. See Install.

items.text:
Item Rain cfnrain Command name rain cfnrain Go module github.com/aws-cloudformation/rain github.com/awesome-foundation/cfnrain User agent that AWS sees Rain/<version> cfnrain/<version> Role session name when cfnrain assumes a role from your profile Rain-<version> cfnrain-<version> Metadata.AWSToolsMetrics block in packaged templates Added Not added. --no-analytics is accepted and has no effect.

If a role trust policy allows only session names that match Rain-*, add cfnrain-*. See Migrating from rain for the full list.

items.title: S3 bucket metadata (experimental)
items.text:
An AWS::S3::Bucket resource can have a Metadata.Rain section. It tells cfnrain deploy and cfnrain rm to do more work around the stack operation: run build scripts, upload files to the bucket, invalidate a CloudFront distribution, and empty the bucket before a delete.

This feature is experimental. If a bucket in the template has Metadata.Rain, deploy and rm stop with metadata commands require the --experimental flag unless you add --experimental.

items.title: Example
items.text:
Resources:
  SiteBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Metadata:
      Rain:
        EmptyOnDelete: true
        Content: site/dist
        DistributionLogicalId: SiteDistribution
        RunBefore:
          Command: build-site.sh
          Args:
            - production
        RunAfter:
          Command: write-config.sh
          Args:
            - Rain::OutputValue ApiUrl

  SiteDistribution:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Properties:
      # ...

Outputs:
  ApiUrl:
    Value: !Sub https://${Api}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/prod

cfnrain deploy site.yaml site-prod --experimental
cfnrain rm site-prod --experimental

items.title: Keys
items.text: Key When What it does RunBefore Before the change set Runs a command. If it fails, the deploy stops. RunAfter After a successful deploy Runs a command. It can use stack outputs as arguments. Content After a successful deploy Uploads every file in a local directory to the bucket DistributionLogicalId After the upload Invalidates all paths in this CloudFront distribution EmptyOnDelete On cfnrain rm Deletes every object and every object version, so CloudFormation can delete the bucket Version Never cfnrain ignores it. Change the number to make the template different, so that a deploy runs the steps again.

items.title: RunBefore and RunAfter
items.text:
Both take a map with Command and an optional Args list. Command is a path relative to the template file. cfnrain runs it in the template's directory. The command must be executable.

In RunAfter, an argument of the form Rain::OutputValue <OutputKey> becomes the value of that stack output. Use it to give a build script the URL of an API that the stack created. RunBefore cannot use Rain::OutputValue, because the stack outputs do not exist yet.

If the command fails, cfnrain prints its output and stops. When it succeeds, cfnrain prints Successfully ran <command>.

items.title: Content
items.text:
Content is a directory, relative to the template file. cfnrain uploads each file with a key that is its path inside that directory. site/dist/css/main.css becomes css/main.css. cfnrain does not delete objects that are no longer in the directory.

An empty value or RAIN_NO_CONTENT skips the upload.

items.title: EmptyOnDelete
items.text: When EmptyOnDelete is true, cfnrain rm asks for confirmation and then deletes all objects in the bucket, also the old versions. With -y it does not ask. Use it for development stacks. Be careful in production.

items.title: Order of steps
items.text:
1. Package the template
  2. RunBefore
  3. Create the change set, confirm, execute and wait
  4. RunAfter
  5. Upload Content
  6. Invalidate DistributionLogicalId

--detach does not wait for the stack

With --detach, cfnrain does not wait for the stack. It runs RunAfter, the upload and the invalidation right away, while CloudFormation is still working. On a new stack the bucket may not exist yet. Do not use --detach with Metadata.Rain.

Templates run code

RunBefore and RunAfter run programs from your computer. Only deploy templates that you trust.

A complete example with modules is in test/webapp.

items.title: AWS console session
items.text:
You came here from the AWS console. cfnrain console signed you in, and this site is the issuer of that sign-in. AWS links back to this page when the console session ends.

To sign in again, run cfnrain console in your terminal.

items.title: CI usage
items.text: cfnrain works in CI without changes. This page shows how to install it in GitHub Actions, how to deploy without questions, and how to show a change set preview on a pull request.

items.title: Install in GitHub Actions
items.text:
Pin the version, download the archive, and check it before you install it:

- name: Install cfnrain
  env:
    CFNRAIN_VERSION: 1.25.2
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  run: |
    cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"
    archive="cfnrain_${CFNRAIN_VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
    gh release download "v${CFNRAIN_VERSION}" -R awesome-foundation/cfnrain \
      -p "$archive" -p checksums.txt
    sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
    gh attestation verify "$archive" -R awesome-foundation/cfnrain
    tar -xzf "$archive" cfnrain
    sudo install cfnrain /usr/local/bin/cfnrain
    cfnrain --version

sha256sum fails the step when the archive does not match checksums.txt. gh attestation verify fails the step when the archive was not built by the cfnrain release workflow. See Install for the details.

items.title: Deploy without questions
items.text:
In CI there is nobody to answer a prompt. Use -y:

cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-prod -y -c config/prod.yaml

With -y:

  • cfnrain does not ask for parameters. Every parameter needs a value from --params, the config file, a RAIN_VAR_* variable, a default, or the existing stack. If one has none, the deploy fails with an error.
  • cfnrain does not show the change set before it executes it.
  • cfnrain creates the artifact bucket if it does not exist.

The exit status is 0 when the stack reaches CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_COMPLETE or IMPORT_COMPLETE, and when there are no changes. Any other result exits with a status that is not 0, so the CI job fails.

--no-colour removes the color codes from the output. This makes CI logs easier to read.

items.title: A complete workflow
items.text:
This workflow checks the format of the templates on every pull request and deploys on every push to main. It uses OpenID Connect to get AWS credentials, so there are no long-lived keys in the repository.

name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

env:
  CFNRAIN_VERSION: 1.25.2

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install cfnrain
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          archive="cfnrain_${CFNRAIN_VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
          gh release download "v${CFNRAIN_VERSION}" -R awesome-foundation/cfnrain \
            -p "$archive" -p checksums.txt
          sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
          tar -xzf "$archive" cfnrain
          sudo install cfnrain /usr/local/bin/cfnrain
      - name: Check template format
        run: cfnrain fmt -v app.yaml

  deploy:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install cfnrain
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          archive="cfnrain_${CFNRAIN_VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
          gh release download "v${CFNRAIN_VERSION}" -R awesome-foundation/cfnrain \
            -p "$archive" -p checksums.txt
          sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
          tar -xzf "$archive" cfnrain
          sudo install cfnrain /usr/local/bin/cfnrain
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/github-deploy
          aws-region: eu-west-1
      - name: Deploy
        run: cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-prod -y -c config/prod.yaml --no-colour

items.title: Change set preview on pull requests
items.text:
A preview shows the reviewers what a pull request will change in the stack, before anybody merges it. Create a change set with --no-exec, read it with the AWS CLI, and post it as a comment.

  preview:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Install cfnrain as in the deploy job
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/github-preview
          aws-region: eu-west-1
      - name: Create the change set
        id: changeset
        run: |
          name="pr-${{ github.event.number }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
          echo "name=$name" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-prod "$name" --no-exec -y -c config/prod.yaml --no-colour | tee deploy.log
      - name: Comment on the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NAME: ${{ steps.changeset.outputs.name }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Change set for app-prod"
            echo
            if grep -q "Deploy was skipped" deploy.log; then
              echo "No changes."
            else
              echo '```'
              aws cloudformation describe-change-set \
                --stack-name app-prod --change-set-name "$NAME" \
                --query 'Changes[].ResourceChange.[Action,LogicalResourceId,ResourceType,Replacement]' \
                --output table
              echo '```'
            fi
          } > preview.md
          gh pr comment "${{ github.event.number }}" --body-file preview.md
      - name: Delete the change set
        if: always()
        run: cfnrain rm -c app-prod "${{ steps.changeset.outputs.name }}" -y || true

Notes:

  • The third argument to deploy names the change set, so the next step can find it. Without it, the name is <stack>-<unix time>.
  • -y stops cfnrain from asking for parameters. --no-exec already skips the confirmation.
  • If the template has no changes, cfnrain prints Deploy was skipped and exits with status 0. The workflow checks for that text. CloudFormation keeps the empty change set with the status FAILED, and the last step deletes it.
  • The Replacement column shows True when CloudFormation will replace a resource. Look for it in the review.
  • Use a role for the preview that can create change sets but cannot execute them.
  • The if condition skips pull requests from forks. Those runs get no AWS credentials, and they should not.
  • For a stack that does not exist yet, the change set leaves an empty stack in REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS. The next cfnrain deploy deletes it without a question. See Getting started.

-x is --no-exec on deploy

On deploy, -x means --no-exec. On other commands, -x means --experimental. Write the long flag names in CI scripts, so the intent is clear.

items.title: Other checks
items.text:
• cfnrain fmt -v <file> fails when a template is not formatted.
  • cfnrain pkg <file> -o packaged.yaml writes the packaged template, so you can run cfn-lint or cfn-guard on it.
  • cfnrain forecast -x <file> <stack> exits with status 1 when a check fails. It is experimental.

Do not run info --creds in CI

cfnrain info --creds prints the secret key and session token. CI logs keep them.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
This page deploys a small stack, changes it, and removes it. It also explains how cfnrain gets parameter and tag values.

You need AWS credentials that can create CloudFormation stacks and S3 buckets. Run cfnrain info to see the account and region that cfnrain uses.

items.title: Your first deploy
items.text:
Save this template as bucket.yaml:

Parameters:
  Env:
    Type: String
    Description: The environment name
    AllowedValues: [dev, prod]

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Env
          Value: !Ref Env

Outputs:
  BucketName:
    Value: !Ref Bucket

Deploy it:

cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml

cfnrain does these steps:

  1. It packages the template. Packaging processes template directives and modules, and uploads local files to the artifact bucket.
  2. It finds the artifact bucket. If the bucket does not exist, cfnrain asks to create it. See Artifact bucket.
  3. It picks the stack name. If you do not give one, the stack name is the template file name without its extension: bucket.

  4. It asks for each parameter that does not have a value from another source:

    Enter a value for parameter 'Env' "The environment name":

    If the parameter has a default or the stack has an existing value, the prompt shows it, and an empty answer keeps it.

  5. It creates a change set and shows it. + is an addition, > is a modification and - is a removal. Nested stacks show under their parent.

    CloudFormation will make the following changes:
Stack bucket:
  + AWS::S3::Bucket Bucket
Do you wish to continue? (Y/n)

  6. If you answer yes, it executes the change set, shows the progress, and prints a summary with the outputs and any failure messages.

If you answer no, cfnrain deletes the change set. If the stack is new, it also deletes the empty stack that CloudFormation created for the change set.

To use a different stack name, give it as the second argument:

cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml billing-dev

items.title: Change the stack
items.text:
Edit the template and run the same command again. cfnrain shows the new change set. If the template has no changes, cfnrain prints Change set was created, but there is no change. Deploy was skipped. and exits with status 0.

On an update, cfnrain asks only for parameters that have no value from the other sources. An empty answer keeps the existing value. cfnrain sends it to CloudFormation as UsePreviousValue.

Failed stacks are deleted without a prompt

If the existing stack is in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, CREATE_FAILED or REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS, cfnrain deletes it before it deploys. It does not ask first, even without -y. Stacks in these states have no working resources. If the stack is in any other state that does not end in _COMPLETE, cfnrain stops with an error.

items.title: Skip the questions with -y
items.text:
-y (--yes) answers yes to every question. cfnrain does not ask for parameters and does not show the change set before it executes it:

cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml billing-dev -y --params Env=dev

With -y, every parameter needs a value from a flag, the config file, an environment variable, a default, or the existing stack. If one has no value, cfnrain stops with this error:

no default or existing value for parameter 'Env'. Set a default, supply a --params flag, or deploy without the --yes flag

items.title: Flags
items.text:
--params sets parameter values and --tags sets stack tags. Both take key=value pairs separated by commas:

cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml --params Env=prod --tags Team=platform,CostCenter=1234

A part with no = belongs to the value before it. --params Subnets=subnet-a,subnet-b sets Subnets to subnet-a,subnet-b. This is how you pass a CommaDelimitedList.

items.title: Config file
items.text:
-c or --config reads parameters and tags from a YAML or JSON file:

Parameters:
  Env: prod
Tags:
  Team: platform
  CostCenter: "1234"

cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml billing-prod -c prod.yaml

The file format is like the AWS CodePipeline template configuration file, without StackPolicy. cfnrain also reads the lowercase keys parameters: and tags:. To get a config file from a stack that is already deployed, run cfnrain cat -c <stack>.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
RAIN_VAR_<Name> sets the parameter <Name>. RAIN_DEFAULT_TAG_<Key> sets the tag <Key>:

export RAIN_VAR_Env=dev
export RAIN_DEFAULT_TAG_Team=platform
cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml -y

Unknown parameters stop the deploy

cfnrain treats every RAIN_VAR_* variable as a parameter. If the template has no parameter with that name, the deploy stops with unknown parameter. Add --ignore-unknown-params to print a warning and continue. The same rule applies to --params and the config file.

items.title: Precedence
items.text:
When a parameter or tag has values from more than one source, cfnrain uses the first one in this list:

  1. --params and --tags
  2. The --config file
  3. RAIN_VAR_* and RAIN_DEFAULT_TAG_* environment variables
  4. Your answer at the prompt. cfnrain asks only when no source above has a value, and only without -y.
  5. The existing value on the stack, for updates
  6. The parameter's Default in the template

When a flag overrides a value from the config file, cfnrain prints a yellow warning.

items.title: Change sets without executing
items.text:
--no-exec creates the change set, prints it, and stops:

cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml billing-prod --no-exec

Changeset contains the following changes:
Stack billing-prod:
  > AWS::S3::Bucket Bucket
changeset created but not executed: billing-prod-1761480000

The default change set name is <stack>-<unix time>. Give a name as the third argument to choose it:

cfnrain deploy bucket.yaml billing-prod release-42 --no-exec

Execute the change set later:

cfnrain deploy --changeset billing-prod release-42

cfnrain ls <stack> lists the change sets of a stack. ls -c shows one change set and rm -c deletes one:

cfnrain ls billing-prod
cfnrain ls -c billing-prod release-42
cfnrain rm -c billing-prod release-42

On deploy, -x means --no-exec

On pkg, forecast, cc and module, -x is short for --experimental. On deploy, -x is short for --no-exec, and --experimental has no short form. cfnrain deploy -x creates a change set and does not execute it.

items.title: Other deploy options
items.text:
Flag What it does -d, --detach Start the deploy and exit. Watch it later with cfnrain watch <stack>. -k, --keep Keep the resources after a failure. This disables rollback. -t, --termination-protection Turn on termination protection after a successful deploy. There is no flag to turn it off. --role-arn The IAM role that CloudFormation assumes to deploy the stack. --nested-change-set=false Do not include nested stacks in the change set. --experimental Allow experimental features, such as S3 bucket metadata and !Rain::Module. --node-style How to write YAML values in the template that cfnrain sends. The values are the same as for fmt --node-style. The default is original. --no-analytics Has no effect. cfnrain keeps it so that old scripts still work. -p, --profile and -r, --region The AWS profile and region

cfnrain always sends the CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM and CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND capabilities. Templates larger than 51,200 bytes go to the artifact bucket first. The limit for those is 1 MB.

The flags for parameters, tags and config files are in Parameters and tags, and the bucket flags are in The artifact bucket. cfnrain deploy --help prints them all.

items.title: Remove the stack
items.text:
cfnrain rm billing-dev

cfnrain shows the stack and asks you to confirm. Add -y to skip the question.

items.title: The artifact bucket
items.text:
cfnrain uploads packaged files and large templates to an S3 bucket. It finds the bucket in this order:

  1. The --s3-bucket flag
  2. The SSM parameter rain-bucket
  3. rain-artifacts-<account id>-<region>

If the bucket does not exist, cfnrain asks to create it. With -y it creates it without a question. You can also create it with cfnrain bootstrap. cfnrain creates the bucket with AES256 encryption, blocks all public access, and adds a lifecycle rule that deletes objects after 7 days. The rule's ID says delete after 14 days, but the real value is 7 days. See Known issues.

--s3-prefix adds a prefix to the object keys. --s3-owner sets the account that must own the bucket. cfnrain sends the owner with every upload, so an upload to a bucket that another account owns fails.

cfnrain resolves the bucket on every deploy, also when the template has nothing to upload.

items.title: Install
items.text: cfnrain is one static binary. Download a release archive, or build it with Go.

items.title: Release archives
items.text:
Each release has archives for Linux, macOS and Windows:

OS Architectures Format Linux amd64, arm64, arm (v7), 386 .tar.gz macOS amd64, arm64 .tar.gz Windows amd64, 386 .zip

The archive name is cfnrain_<version>_<os>_<arch>, for example cfnrain_1.25.2_linux_amd64.tar.gz. Each archive contains cfnrain, LICENSE, NOTICE and README.md. Each release also has a checksums.txt file.

Download an archive and the checksum file. This example uses the GitHub CLI:

VERSION=1.25.2
gh release download "v${VERSION}" -R awesome-foundation/cfnrain \
  -p "cfnrain_${VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" -p checksums.txt

You can also download them from the release page with a browser or curl.

items.title: Verify the checksum
items.text:
checksums.txt lists the SHA-256 checksum of every archive. Check the archive that you downloaded:

sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt

The output must say OK for your archive. On macOS, use shasum -a 256 --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt.

items.title: Verify the provenance
items.text:
The release workflow attests the build provenance of every archive. The attestation proves that the archive was built by the cfnrain release workflow from this repository. Verify it with the GitHub CLI:

gh attestation verify "cfnrain_${VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" -R awesome-foundation/cfnrain

items.title: Install the binary
items.text:
tar -xzf "cfnrain_${VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" cfnrain
sudo install cfnrain /usr/local/bin/cfnrain
cfnrain --version

cfnrain --version prints the version, the OS and the architecture, for example cfnrain v1.25.2 linux/amd64.

items.title: Install with Go
items.text:
If you have Go installed, build and install the latest release:

go install github.com/awesome-foundation/cfnrain/cmd/cfnrain@latest

Go puts the binary in $(go env GOPATH)/bin. Make sure that this directory is on your PATH.

items.title: Homebrew
items.text: There is no Homebrew formula yet. Follow issue #14 for progress.

items.title: Keep the rain name
items.text:
Scripts that call rain keep working when you link the name to cfnrain:

ln -s "$(command -v cfnrain)" /usr/local/bin/rain

You can use any directory on your PATH. Shell completion can complete both names.

items.title: Shell completion
items.text:
cfnrain completion prints a completion script for bash, zsh, fish or PowerShell. cfnrain completion <shell> --help shows more ways to install it.

# bash: add this line to ~/.bashrc
source <(cfnrain completion bash)

# zsh: add this line to ~/.zshrc, after compinit
source <(cfnrain completion zsh)

# fish
cfnrain completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/cfnrain.fish

If you linked rain to cfnrain, add a second line to complete that name too:

# bash
complete -o default -F __start_cfnrain rain

# zsh
compdef _cfnrain rain

items.title: AWS credentials
items.text:
cfnrain uses the standard AWS SDK credential chain: environment variables, the shared config and credentials files, SSO, and instance or container roles. Use -p or --profile to pick a profile and -r or --region to pick a region.

Check which account and region cfnrain uses:

cfnrain info

items.title: Known issues
items.text: These are places where cfnrain does something unexpected. They come from Rain, and cfnrain has not fixed them yet. Each one says what to do instead.

items.title: A !Sub constant inside another !Sub packages to an empty value
items.text:
A Rain: constant that is itself a !Sub string, used with ${Rain::<Name>} inside another !Sub, packages to an empty string. There is no error.

Use !Rain::Constant <Name> for that constant instead. See Constants.

items.title: Fn::Select takes its arguments in the reverse order
items.text: cfnrain simplifies Fn::Select only when the list comes first and the index second. CloudFormation uses the index first. Write Fn::Select in the CloudFormation order. cfnrain then leaves it for CloudFormation, which resolves it. See Intrinsic functions.

items.title: build --only-cache does the same as --no-cache
items.text: cfnrain build --only-cache should use only the cached schemas. In the code it sets the same switch as --no-cache, so it skips the cache. Do not rely on --only-cache.

items.title: The artifact bucket deletes objects after 7 days, not 14
items.text:
When cfnrain creates the artifact bucket, it adds a lifecycle rule with the ID delete after 14 days. The rule deletes objects, old object versions and incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.

CloudFormation does not need the uploaded files after a deploy. But if you deploy an old change set or roll back to a template after more than 7 days, the files can be gone. The cc state files are in the same bucket and expire too. Use --s3-bucket with your own bucket if you need to keep objects longer.

items.title: info --creds prints the secret key
items.text: cfnrain info --creds prints the SecretAccessKey and the SessionToken in plain text. Do not run it where other people or logs can see the output.

items.title: Failed stacks are deleted without a prompt
items.text: If a stack is in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, CREATE_FAILED or REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS, cfnrain deploy deletes it before it deploys, also without -y. See Getting started.

items.title: Implicit uploads fail without an error
items.text: If an implicit upload fails, for example because the local path does not exist, cfnrain leaves the path in the template and continues. CloudFormation then fails on the path. Run cfnrain pkg --debug to see the reason.

items.title: The pkg help text lists the wrong S3 Format values
items.text: cfnrain pkg --help lists Format: Uri|Http. The code expects URI, Http or Object, and Object is the default when you set both BucketProperty and KeyProperty. The help text also leaves out the Run and Extension options. See S3 and S3Http for the correct values.

items.title: The stackset deploy help text says the template is optional
items.text: cfnrain stackset deploy --help says that without a template file, cfnrain adds a new instance to an existing stack set. The code always reads the first argument as the template file, so you must give one.

items.title: Things that do not exist
items.text:
Older Rain documentation describes these, but the code does not have them:

  • SourceMap metadata on packaged resources
  • A VersionProperty option for !Rain::S3
  • Pkl input for diff, merge and tree
  • The $MapValue placeholder in ForEach
  • The ModuleExtension resource and Metadata.Extends for !Rain::Module

If you find another difference between this site and the code, please open an issue.

items.title: Migrating from rain
items.text: cfnrain starts from Rain v1.24.4 plus 22 later commits. Templates, config files, environment variables and the artifact bucket work as before. Most migrations only change the name of the binary.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Install cfnrain.

  2. Replace rain with cfnrain in your scripts and CI workflows. Or link the old name, so the scripts do not change:

    ln -s "$(command -v cfnrain)" /usr/local/bin/rain

  3. If an IAM role trust policy limits the session name, allow cfnrain-*. See Role session name.

  4. Remove the Rain binary or the Homebrew formula when you no longer need it.

items.title: What stays the same
items.text: Item Status !Rain::* directives Same The Rain: template section Same The Modules, Packages and Constants sections Same Metadata.Rain on S3 buckets Same Config files for --config Same RAIN_VAR_* and RAIN_DEFAULT_TAG_* Same Artifact bucket rain-artifacts-<account>-<region> Same bucket, cfnrain uses it as it is SSM parameter rain-bucket Same cc state files in the artifact bucket Same location CodeArtifact defaults for module (--domain cloudformation, --repo rain) Same Flags and commands Same

items.title: Binary and module name
items.text:
The command is cfnrain. The Go module is github.com/awesome-foundation/cfnrain. go install uses the new path:

go install github.com/awesome-foundation/cfnrain/cmd/cfnrain@latest

cfnrain --version prints cfnrain v<version> <os>/<arch>. Scripts that parse the version output need an update.

items.title: User agent
items.text: AWS sees the user agent cfnrain/<version>, not Rain/<version>. If you filter CloudTrail events or write IAM conditions on the user agent, update them.

items.title: Role session name
items.text:
When cfnrain assumes a role from your AWS profile, the role session name is cfnrain-<version>, not Rain-<version>. If a role trust policy only allows session names that match Rain-*, add cfnrain-*:

"Condition": {
  "StringLike": {
    "sts:RoleSessionName": ["Rain-*", "cfnrain-*"]
  }
}

items.title: No analytics metadata
items.text: Rain added a Metadata.AWSToolsMetrics.Rain block to every packaged template. cfnrain does not. The --no-analytics flag is still accepted, and has no effect. If you compare packaged templates from Rain and cfnrain, expect this block to be the difference.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
The Rain documentation at aws-cloudformation.github.io/rain is frozen. This site replaces it. Some things that the old README said were wrong:

  • On deploy, -x is --no-exec, not --experimental. See Getting started.
  • The Modules section does not need --experimental. Only !Rain::Module and bucket metadata do.
  • !Rain::S3 takes Format: URI, not Uri. See S3.
  • The ForEach placeholders are $Identifier and $Index. There is no $MapValue. See ForEach.
  • Packaged resources get no SourceMap metadata.
  • !Rain::Module does not need a ModuleExtension resource or Metadata.Extends.

See Known issues for behavior that is still wrong in the code.

items.title: Pkl
items.text: Pkl is a configuration language from Apple. cfnrain can read templates written in Pkl, and can write templates as Pkl.

items.title: Requirements
items.text: cfnrain runs Pkl through the pkl command line tool. Install it from the Pkl website and make sure that it is on your PATH.

items.title: Read Pkl templates
items.text:
pkg, deploy and fmt accept a file with the .pkl extension. cfnrain evaluates it to YAML first, and then works with the YAML.

cfnrain fmt template.pkl
cfnrain deploy template.pkl my-stack

diff, merge and tree do not read Pkl files. Run cfnrain fmt template.pkl > template.yaml first.

A Pkl template that uses the cloudformation-pkl package:

amends "package://github.com/aws-cloudformation/cloudformation-pkl/releases/download/cloudformation@0.1.1/cloudformation@0.1.1#/template.pkl"
import "package://github.com/aws-cloudformation/cloudformation-pkl/releases/download/cloudformation@0.1.1/cloudformation@0.1.1#/cloudformation.pkl" as cfn
import "package://github.com/aws-cloudformation/cloudformation-pkl/releases/download/cloudformation@0.1.1/cloudformation@0.1.1#/aws/s3/bucket.pkl" as bucket

Description = "Create a bucket"

Parameters {
    ["Name"] {
        Type = "String"
        Default = "baz"
    }
}

Resources {
    ["MyBucket"] = new bucket.Bucket {
        BucketName = cfn.Ref("Name")
    }
}

The cloudformation-pkl package is an AWS project. cfnrain does not maintain it.

items.title: Write Pkl
items.text:
cfnrain fmt -p converts a YAML or JSON template to Pkl:

cfnrain fmt -p template.yaml > template.pkl
Flag What it does -p, --pkl Write Pkl --pkl-basic Do not use the Pkl modules for each resource type --pkl-package The alias or URI of the Pkl package to import. The default is @cfn.

cfnrain build --pkl-class <type> writes a Pkl class for a resource type.

A full example is in test/webapp, in webapp.pkl.

items.title: Other commands
items.text:
These commands do not work with templates or stacks directly. Both take -p (--profile) and -r (--region). Both also take --debug and --no-colour, and print their usage with -h (--help).

The output on these pages is illustrative. It needs a real AWS account.

Command What it does info Shows the account, region, identity and profile that cfnrain uses. console Makes a sign-in URL for the AWS console from your current credentials and opens it in a browser.

items.title: console
items.text:
cfnrain console makes a sign-in URL for the AWS console from your current credentials and opens it in a browser.

# Open the CloudFormation console
cfnrain console

# Open the CloudFormation console with a stack selected
cfnrain console app-prod

# Open another service
cfnrain console -s lambda

# Print the URL and do not open a browser
cfnrain console -u
Flag What it does -s, --service The service home page to open. The default is cloudformation. cfnrain selects the stack only on the cloudformation page. -u, --url Print the URL only -n, --name The user name to show in the console. The default comes from the role name. -l, --logout Sign out of the AWS console

console works only with IAM role credentials, not with IAM user credentials.

The sign-in URL names https://awesome-foundation.github.io/cfnrain/cfnrain_console.html as the issuer. When your console session expires, AWS links back to that page.

items.title: info
items.text:
cfnrain info shows the account, region, identity and profile that cfnrain uses.

cfnrain info

Account:  123456789012
Region:   eu-west-1
Identity: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/Developer/jane

-c (--creds) also prints the credential source and the credentials.

--creds prints your secret key

cfnrain info --creds prints the SecretAccessKey and the SessionToken in plain text. Do not run it in CI logs, screen shares or recorded terminals.

items.title: Stack commands
items.text:
These commands work with deployed CloudFormation stacks. All of them take -p (--profile) and -r (--region). Every command also takes --debug and --no-colour, and prints its usage with -h (--help).

The command output on these pages is illustrative. It needs a real AWS account, so the names, IDs and times in your output will be different.

Command What it does deploy Creates or updates a stack through a change set. ls Lists the stacks in the current region. cat Prints the template of a deployed stack. logs Shows the events of a stack and its nested stacks. watch Shows the status of a stack while it changes. rm Deletes a stack and waits until the delete completes. stackset Works with CloudFormation stack sets. cc Deploys templates with the Cloud Control API instead of CloudFormation. Experimental.

items.title: cat
items.text:
cfnrain cat <stack> prints the template of a deployed stack. cfnrain formats it like fmt does.

cfnrain cat app-prod
Flag What it prints -t, --transformed The template after CloudFormation processed transforms such as AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31 -u, --unformatted The template as CloudFormation stores it, with no formatting -c, --config A config file with the stack's parameters and tags, in the format that deploy --config reads

Use -c to copy the settings of one stack to a new deploy:

cfnrain cat -c app-prod > prod.yaml
cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-prod -c prod.yaml

items.title: cc (experimental)
items.text:
cfnrain cc deploys templates with the Cloud Control API instead of CloudFormation. Every cc command needs -x (--experimental).

cfnrain cc deploy -x app.yaml app-dev
cfnrain cc state -x app-dev
cfnrain cc drift -x app-dev
cfnrain cc rm -x app-dev
Subcommand What it does cc deploy <template> <name> Creates or updates the resources. It refuses resource types that the Cloud Control API does not fully support. cc state <name> Prints the state file cc drift <name> Compares the state file with the live resources, and offers to fix the difference cc rm <name> Deletes the resources and waits until all the Cloud Control API calls complete

cc keeps a state file in the artifact bucket at deployments/<name>.yaml. If a deploy stops and leaves a lock, cc deploy -u <lockid> removes the lock.

Flag Subcommands What it does -x, --experimental all Confirm that you know cc is experimental. Required. --s3-bucket, --s3-prefix all The bucket and prefix of the state file and the uploads --s3-owner cc The account that owns the bucket --params deploy Parameter values, in the format key1=value1,key2=value2 --tags deploy Tags, in the format key1=value1,key2=value2 -c, --config deploy A YAML or JSON file with parameters and tags, as for deploy --ignore-unknown-params deploy Ignore parameters that the template does not declare -u, --unlock deploy Remove the lock with this ID and continue -y, --yes deploy, rm Do not ask questions

State files expire in buckets that cfnrain creates

The artifact bucket that cfnrain creates deletes all objects after 7 days. That includes the cc state files. Use --s3-bucket with a bucket that keeps its objects.

items.title: deploy
items.text:
cfnrain deploy <template> [stack] [changeset] creates or updates a stack through a change set. Getting started explains the full flow, parameters, config files and change sets.

# Deploy, with a prompt for each parameter and a confirmation
cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-dev

# Deploy without questions
cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-prod -y -c prod.yaml

# Create a change set and stop
cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-prod --no-exec

Getting started lists every deploy flag.

items.title: logs
items.text:
cfnrain logs <stack> shows the events of a stack and its nested stacks. By default it shows only the events with a useful message, such as a failure reason. log is an alias.

cfnrain logs app-prod

Give a logical resource ID to see the events of one resource:

cfnrain logs app-prod Bucket
Flag What it does -a, --all Show all events, also the ones without a useful message -l, --length Show only this number of events -d, --days Show only the events from the last number of days -s, --since-user-initiated Show only the events since the last User Initiated event -c, --chart Write an HTML Gantt chart of the most recent stack operation to standard output

The chart shows how long each resource took. Save it to a file and open it in a browser:

cfnrain logs --chart app-prod > chart.html

items.title: ls
items.text:
cfnrain ls lists the stacks in the current region. Add -a (--all) to list the stacks in all regions.

cfnrain ls
cfnrain ls -a

Give a stack name to see a summary of that stack and its change sets. With -a, the summary has more detail.

cfnrain ls app-prod

-c (--changeset) works with change sets. With no arguments it lists the stacks that have change sets. With a stack and a change set name it shows that change set.

cfnrain ls -c
cfnrain ls -c app-prod release-42

list is an alias for ls.

items.title: rm
items.text:
cfnrain rm <stack> deletes a stack and waits until the delete completes. It asks you to confirm first. remove, del and delete are aliases.

cfnrain rm app-dev
cfnrain rm app-dev -y

If the stack has termination protection, cfnrain asks whether to turn it off. With -y it turns it off without a question.

Flag What it does -y, --yes Do not ask questions -d, --detach Start the delete and exit --role-arn The IAM role that CloudFormation assumes to delete the stack -c, --changeset Delete a change set instead of a stack: cfnrain rm -c <stack> <changeset> --experimental Needed when a bucket in the stack has Metadata.Rain

items.title: stackset
items.text: cfnrain stackset works with CloudFormation stack sets. It has three subcommands. All of them take --admin to use delegated administrator permissions.

items.title: stackset deploy
items.text:
cfnrain stackset deploy <template> [stackset] creates or updates a stack set. If you do not give a name, the stack set name is the template file name without its extension.

cfnrain stackset deploy guardrails.yaml org-guardrails \
  --accounts 111111111111,222222222222 \
  --regions us-east-1,eu-west-1 \
  --params Env=prod

The config file can set the stack set and the instances, as well as parameters and tags:

Parameters:
  Env: prod
Tags:
  Team: platform
StackSet:
  description: Organization guardrails
StackSetInstances:
  accounts:
    - "111111111111"
  regions:
    - us-east-1

Accounts and regions from the flags replace the values from the file. Tags and parameters from the flags are merged with the values from the file. -i (--ignore-stack-instances) updates the stack set and does not add or remove instances. See test-config.yaml for a full config file.

Like deploy, stackset deploy packages the template first, and creates the artifact bucket when it needs one.

Flag What it does --accounts The accounts to create stack set instances in, separated by commas --regions The regions to create stack set instances in, separated by commas --params Parameter values, in the format key1=value1,key2=value2 --tags Tags, in the format key1=value1,key2=value2 -c, --config A YAML or JSON config file, as shown above -i, --ignore-stack-instances Update the stack set and do not add or remove instances -y, --yes Do not ask for confirmation -d, --detach Start the operation and exit --admin Use delegated administrator permissions --s3-bucket, --s3-prefix, --s3-owner Control where uploads go. See Artifact bucket.

items.title: stackset ls
items.text:
cfnrain stackset ls lists the stack sets in the region. Give a name to see its instances and its last 10 operations.

cfnrain stackset ls
cfnrain stackset ls org-guardrails

-a (--all) lists the stack sets in all regions. With a name, it shows more detail.

items.title: stackset rm
items.text:
cfnrain stackset rm <stackset> deletes a stack set. If the stack set still has instances, cfnrain lists them and asks which ones to delete. Enter 0 to delete all of them.

cfnrain stackset rm org-guardrails

-d (--detach) starts the delete and exits.

items.title: watch
items.text:
cfnrain watch <stack> shows the status of a stack while it changes. Use it for a deploy that another tool started, or after deploy --detach.

cfnrain deploy app.yaml app-prod -y --detach
cfnrain watch app-prod

If the stack is not changing, watch stops with an error. Add -w (--wait) to wait until a change starts.

items.title: Template commands
items.text:
These commands work with template files on your computer. diff, fmt, merge and tree need no AWS credentials. pkg, bootstrap, build, forecast and module can call AWS, so they take -p (--profile) and -r (--region). Every command also takes --debug and --no-colour, and prints its usage with -h (--help).

The output on these pages comes from real runs of cfnrain, unless a page says otherwise.

Command What it does fmt Formats templates. pkg Packages a template. diff Compares two template files. merge Merges two or more templates into one. tree Shows which parameters, resources and outputs depend on each other. build Makes starter templates from the CloudFormation resource schemas. bootstrap Creates the artifact bucket. forecast Looks for things that can make a deploy fail, such as a bucket name that already exists or an EC2 key pair that does not exist. Experimental. module Publishes and installs packages of modules with AWS CodeArtifact. Experimental.

items.title: bootstrap
items.text:
cfnrain bootstrap creates the artifact bucket. deploy and pkg create it too when they need it, so you only need bootstrap to create it ahead of time.

cfnrain bootstrap
cfnrain bootstrap -y --s3-bucket my-artifacts

-y (--yes) creates the bucket without asking. --s3-bucket, --s3-prefix and --s3-owner work as for pkg. See Artifact bucket for the bucket name and settings.

items.title: build
items.text:
cfnrain build makes starter templates from the CloudFormation resource schemas. The schemas are in the binary, so most uses need no AWS call.

Make a template with only the required properties of a type:

cfnrain build -b AWS::SQS::Queue

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: 2010-09-09

Description: Generated by rain

Resources:
  Queue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties: {}

Without -b, the template has every property that you can set. You can give more than one type.

List the resource types that start with a prefix:

cfnrain build -l AWS::SQS

AWS::SQS::Queue
AWS::SQS::QueueInlinePolicy
AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy
Flag What it does -b, --bare Only the required properties -j, --json JSON instead of YAML -s, --schema Print the registry schema of a type -l, --list List resource types, with an optional prefix -o, --output Write to a file --recommend Print a recommended template for a use case. With no more arguments, cfnrain shows a menu. cfnrain build --recommend bucket bucket prints the recommended bucket template. --pkl-class Print a Pkl class for a type --prompt Write a template with Amazon Bedrock from a text prompt. The default model is claude2, which is old. Bedrock usage costs money. --model The Bedrock model ID for --prompt. The short names claude2, claude3haiku, claude3sonnet, claude3opus and claude3.5sonnet also work. --prompt-lang What --prompt writes: cfn (CloudFormation YAML, the default), guard (CloudFormation Guard) or rego (Open Policy Agent Rego) --omit-patches Use the raw registry schema. By default, cfnrain applies its own fixes to the schemas. --no-cache Do not use the schemas in the binary. Get them from the CloudFormation registry. --only-cache Meant to use only the schemas in the binary. See the warning below.

With no arguments, build shows an interactive menu.

--only-cache does the same as --no-cache

In the code, --only-cache sets the same switch as --no-cache. Both make cfnrain skip the cached schemas. See Known issues.

items.title: diff
items.text:
cfnrain diff <from> <to> compares two template files.

cfnrain diff old.yaml new.yaml

(|) Resources:
(|)   Bucket:
(|)     Properties:
(|)       BucketName:
(>)         Fn::Sub: ${AWS::StackName}-files
(+)   Queue:
(+)     Type: AWS::SQS::Queue

(+) is an addition, (-) is a removal, (>) is a change and (|) is a parent of a change. -l (--long) also shows the parts that did not change. diff compares two local files. It does not compare a file with a deployed stack.

items.title: fmt
items.text:
cfnrain fmt formats templates. It sorts the sections and properties in a fixed order, uses the short form of intrinsic functions (!Sub, !Ref), and keeps your YAML comments. format is an alias.

Input, bucket.json:

{"Resources":{"Bucket":{"Properties":{"BucketName":{"Fn::Sub":"${AWS::StackName}-data"}},"Type":"AWS::S3::Bucket"}},"Outputs":{"Name":{"Value":{"Ref":"Bucket"}}}}

cfnrain fmt bucket.json

Output:

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-data

Outputs:
  Name:
    Value: !Ref Bucket
Flag What it does -w, --write Write the result back to the file -v, --verify Do not print. Exit with status 0 if the file is already formatted, and 1 if it is not. -j, --json Write JSON instead of YAML -u, --unsorted Keep the original order of sections and properties --uncdk Remove CDK metadata, simplify logical IDs, and turn Fn::Join into Fn::Sub --node-style Choose how to write YAML values: tagged, doublequoted, singlequoted, literal, folded, strict-boolean, quotescalars, original or flow -p, --pkl Write Pkl instead of YAML --pkl-basic With --pkl, do not use the Pkl modules of the cfn package --pkl-package With --pkl, the alias or full URI of the Pkl package. The default is @cfn. --datamodel Print the internal YAML data model. This is for debugging cfnrain.

With no file names, fmt reads standard input.

Format every template in place:

cfnrain fmt -w templates/*.yaml

Fail a CI job when a template is not formatted:

cfnrain fmt -v templates/app.yaml

templates/app.yaml: would reformat

--verify compares the input text with the formatted YAML. A JSON file never passes unless you also give -j.

items.title: forecast (experimental)
items.text:
cfnrain forecast looks for things that can make a deploy fail, such as a bucket name that already exists or an EC2 key pair that does not exist. It is not a linter. Use cfn-lint to check the syntax. It needs -x (--experimental).

cfnrain forecast -x app.yaml app-prod

The output in this example is illustrative. When a check fails, it looks like this:

Stormy weather ahead! 🌪

1 checks failed out of 9 total checks
FG001 FAIL on line 6: AWS::S3::Bucket Bucket - Resource with this name already exists

When all checks pass, the output starts with Clear skies! and the number of checks. The exit status is 1 when a check fails, so you can use forecast in CI.

Flag What it does --action create, update, delete or all (default) -a, --all Show all checks, not only the failed ones --include-iam Also check IAM permissions. This is slow. --role-arn The role to use for the IAM checks --type Check only one resource type --ignore Skip resource types or check codes, for example AWS::S3::Bucket,F0002 --params, --tags, -c (--config) Parameter and tag values, as for deploy --plugin The path to a forecast plugin .so file with more checks. The release binaries cannot load plugins. See #13. --plugin-only Run only the plugin checks, not the built-in ones

The checks cover S3 buckets and bucket policies, EC2 instances, launch templates and security groups, RDS clusters, load balancer listeners and target groups, SNS topics, Lambda functions and SageMaker notebook instances.

items.title: merge
items.text:
cfnrain merge merges two or more templates into one.

cfnrain merge bucket.yaml queue.yaml

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-data

  Queue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue

If two templates use the same logical ID, merge stops with an error. -f (--force) renames the second one instead. It does not update the Ref, GetAtt and Sub references to the renamed item. --merge-imports replaces an Fn::ImportValue with a direct reference when the export comes from another template in the merge. -o (--output) writes the result to a file. --node-style sets how to write YAML values, as for fmt.

items.title: module (experimental)
items.text: cfnrain module publishes and installs packages of modules with AWS CodeArtifact. See Packages.

items.title: pkg
items.text:
cfnrain pkg <template> packages a template. It processes the template directives, modules and implicit uploads, and prints the result. It is like aws cloudformation package, with more features. package is an alias.

cfnrain pkg app.yaml -o app.packaged.yaml

deploy and forecast package the template too, so you only need pkg to see or keep the packaged template. Run linters such as cfn-lint on the packaged template, because they do not know the cfnrain directives.

Flag What it does -o, --output Write the result to a file -x, --experimental Allow !Rain::Module --s3-bucket, --s3-prefix, --s3-owner Control where uploads go. See Artifact bucket. --node-style How to write YAML values, as for fmt --datamodel Print the internal YAML data model. This is for debugging cfnrain. --no-analytics Has no effect. cfnrain keeps it so that old scripts still work.

items.title: tree
items.text:
cfnrain tree <template> shows which parameters, resources and outputs depend on each other. graph is an alias.

cfnrain tree bucket.yaml

Resources:
  Bucket:
    DependsOn:
      Parameters:
        - AWS::StackName
Outputs:
  Name:
    DependsOn:
      Resources:
        - Bucket

-b (--both) also shows what depends on each item. -a (--all) shows items with no dependencies. -d (--dot) writes the graph in GraphViz DOT format:

cfnrain tree -d bucket.yaml | dot -Tsvg > bucket.svg

items.title: Template directives
items.text:
Directives are YAML tags that start with !Rain::. cfnrain processes them when it packages a template, and replaces each one with a plain value. CloudFormation never sees them.

These commands package templates: pkg, deploy, forecast, stackset deploy and cc deploy. Run cfnrain pkg to see the packaged template before you deploy it.

Directive What it inserts Needs AWS !Rain::Embed <path> The contents of a file, as a string No !Rain::Include <path> A YAML or JSON file, as an object No !Rain::Env <name> The value of an environment variable, as a string No !Rain::S3 <path> The S3 URI of an uploaded file, or an object with the bucket and key Yes !Rain::S3Http <path> The HTTPS URL of an uploaded file Yes !Rain::Constant <name> The value of a constant from the Rain: section No !Rain::Module <uri> The resources of a module. This is the older module system and needs --experimental. No

cfnrain also uploads local files for some resource properties without a directive, like aws cloudformation package does. See Implicit uploads.

items.title: Paths
items.text: A path in a directive is relative to the directory of the template file that contains it. It is not relative to the directory where you run cfnrain. In an included file or a module, paths are relative to that file.

items.title: Long form
items.text:
The YAML tag is a short form. The long form is a map with one key, and it also works in JSON templates:

{
  "Code": {
    "ZipFile": { "Rain::Embed": "handler.py" }
  }
}

items.title: Examples come from tests
items.text: The examples on these pages are test files in cft/pkg/tmpl/docs. go test ./cft/pkg/ packages each -template.yaml file and compares the result with its -expect.yaml file. If cfnrain changes how a directive works, the test fails. The S3 directives need AWS, so their examples are illustrative and not tested.

items.title: Constants and !Rain::Constant
items.text:
The Rain: section of a template can hold constants. A constant is a value that you write once and use in many places. cfnrain removes the Rain: section when it packages the template.

Rain:
  Constants:
    App: billing

Use a constant in two ways:

  • !Rain::Constant <Name> inserts the value. The value can be a string or an object.
  • ${Rain::<Name>} inside a !Sub string inserts a string value.

A constant can use the constants above it, with ${Rain::<Name>} in a !Sub. If a !Sub has no variables left after cfnrain inserts the constants, cfnrain replaces it with a plain string.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The template:

Parameters:
  Env:
    Type: String

Rain:
  Constants:
    App: billing
    Prefix: !Sub ${Env}-${Rain::App}

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub ${Env}-${Rain::App}-uploads
  Table:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Rain::Constant Prefix

The packaged template:

Parameters:
  Env:
    Type: String

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub ${Env}-billing-uploads
  Table:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub ${Env}-billing

${Env} stays in the output, because it is a template parameter that CloudFormation resolves.

items.title: Known issue: a !Sub constant inside another !Sub
items.text:
This packages to an empty value

If a constant is itself a !Sub string, do not use it with ${Rain::<Name>} inside another !Sub. cfnrain packages it to an empty string and shows no error.

Rain:
  Constants:
    Prefix: !Sub ${Env}-billing
Resources:
  Table:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub ${Rain::Prefix}-orders   # packages to "-orders"

Use !Rain::Constant Prefix instead, as in the example above. That works.

items.title: The Constants section
items.text: Templates and modules can also have a top-level Constants: section, with ${Const::<Name>} and !Ref Const::<Name>. That section belongs to the module system. See Constants section.

items.title: !Rain::Embed
items.text:
!Rain::Embed <path> reads a file and inserts its contents into the template as a string. cfnrain removes the whitespace at the start and end of the file. The path must be a file, not a directory.

Use it for inline Lambda code, scripts, policies in a text format, and other text that is easier to edit in its own file.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The template:

Resources:
  Function:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.main
      Role: !GetAtt FunctionRole.Arn
      Code:
        ZipFile: !Rain::Embed handler.py

handler.py, in the same directory:

import json


def main(event, context):
    return {"statusCode": 200, "body": json.dumps({"ok": True})}

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Function:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.main
      Role: !GetAtt FunctionRole.Arn
      Code:
        ZipFile: |-
          import json


          def main(event, context):
              return {"statusCode": 200, "body": json.dumps({"ok": True})}

items.title: Related
items.text:
• !Rain::Include parses the file as YAML or JSON and inserts an object, not a string.
  • Fn::InsertFile also inserts a file as a string. Unlike !Rain::Embed, it keeps the whitespace at the end.

items.title: !Rain::Env
items.text:
!Rain::Env <name> inserts the value of an environment variable into the template as a string. If the variable is not set, packaging stops with the error missing environmental variable.

Use it for values that come from the build system, such as a commit ID or the name of the pipeline that deploys the stack.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The template:

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: DeployedBy
          Value: !Rain::Env DEPLOYED_BY

The packaged template, with DEPLOYED_BY=ci-pipeline in the environment:

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: DeployedBy
          Value: ci-pipeline

Parameters are often a better fit

The value is fixed in the packaged template. CloudFormation does not see where it came from. For values that change between environments, a template parameter with RAIN_VAR_<Name> shows the value in the stack parameters.

items.title: Implicit uploads
items.text:
Some resource properties take an S3 location. If the template has a local path in one of these properties, cfnrain uploads the file and replaces the path with the S3 location. You do not need a directive. This is what aws cloudformation package does too.

Illustrative output

Uploads need AWS, so the output on this page is illustrative.

items.title: Example
items.text:
Resources:
  Function:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.main
      Role: !GetAtt FunctionRole.Arn
      Code: lambda-src

  Network:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
    Properties:
      TemplateURL: network.yaml

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Function:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.main
      Role: !GetAtt FunctionRole.Arn
      Code:
        S3Bucket: rain-artifacts-123456789012-eu-west-1
        S3Key: 1b4844dacc843f09941c11c94f80981d3be8ae7578952c71e875ef7add37b1a7

  Network:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
    Properties:
      TemplateURL: https://rain-artifacts-123456789012-eu-west-1.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/d2a84f4b8b650937ec8f73cd8be2c74add5a911ba64df27458ed8229da804a26

items.title: Properties
items.text: Resource type Property Output AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi BodyS3Location Object with Bucket and Key AWS::AppSync::FunctionConfiguration RequestMappingTemplateS3Location, ResponseMappingTemplateS3Location S3 URI AWS::AppSync::GraphQLSchema DefinitionS3Location S3 URI AWS::AppSync::Resolver RequestMappingTemplateS3Location, ResponseMappingTemplateS3Location S3 URI AWS::CloudFormation::Stack TemplateURL HTTPS URL. cfnrain packages the nested template first. AWS::ElasticBeanstalk::ApplicationVersion SourceBundle Object with S3Bucket and S3Key AWS::Glue::Job Command.ScriptLocation S3 URI AWS::Lambda::Function Code Object with S3Bucket and S3Key, always zipped AWS::Lambda::LayerVersion Content Object with S3Bucket and S3Key, always zipped AWS::Serverless::Api DefinitionUri S3 URI AWS::Serverless::Application Location HTTPS URL. cfnrain packages the nested template first. AWS::Serverless::Function CodeUri S3 URI, always zipped AWS::Serverless::LayerVersion ContentUri S3 URI, always zipped AWS::ServerlessRepo::Application LicenseUrl, ReadmeUrl S3 URI AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine DefinitionS3Location Object with Bucket and Key

items.title: Rules
items.text:
• cfnrain only changes a value that is a plain string. A map, such as an existing S3Bucket and S3Key, stays as it is.
  • An S3 URI (s3://...) stays as it is. For the nested stack properties, an http:// or https:// URL stays as it is.
  • If the upload fails, for example because the path does not exist, cfnrain leaves the value as it is and shows no error. Run with --debug to see why. The nested stack properties are different: a missing nested template stops packaging.
  • Nested templates are packaged with all their directives and modules, then uploaded.

The AWS CLI also packages AWS::Include Location, AWS::Serverless::StateMachine DefinitionUri and AWS::CodeCommit::Repository Code.S3. cfnrain does not. Use !Rain::S3 for those.

items.title: !Rain::Include
items.text:
!Rain::Include <path> reads a YAML or JSON file and inserts it into the template as an object. cfnrain also processes the directives in the included file. Paths in the included file are relative to that file.

Use it to share tags, policies, or whole resource definitions between templates.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The template:

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      Tags: !Rain::Include tags.yaml

tags.yaml, in the same directory:

- Key: Team
  Value: platform
- Key: CostCenter
  Value: "1234"

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Team
          Value: platform
        - Key: CostCenter
          Value: "1234"

items.title: Related
items.text:
• !Rain::Embed inserts a file as a string.
  • Modules insert a group of resources, with parameters and outputs.

items.title: !Rain::S3 and !Rain::S3Http
items.text:
These directives upload a local file or directory to the artifact bucket and insert its location into the template.

Illustrative output

These directives upload to S3, so the tests cannot run them without AWS. The packaged output on this page is illustrative. Your bucket name and object keys will be different.

items.title: How uploads work
items.text:
• If the path is a directory, cfnrain zips it first. Zip: true also zips a single file.
  • The object key is the SHA-256 hash of the content that cfnrain uploads, as hex. If you set --s3-prefix, the key starts with that prefix. Extension adds a file extension.
  • A file that did not change gets the same key, so CloudFormation sees no change. A zip file also stores the modification time of each file. If a build or a fresh checkout touches the files, the zip gets a new key, and CloudFormation updates the resource.
  • Paths are relative to the template file.
  • cfnrain uploads each path only once per run, also when the template uses it many times.

items.title: !Rain::S3
items.text:
The short form takes a path and inserts the S3 URI:

Resources:
  Job:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Job
    Properties:
      Command:
        Name: glueetl
        ScriptLocation: !Rain::S3 etl/job.py

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Job:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Job
    Properties:
      Command:
        Name: glueetl
        ScriptLocation: s3://rain-artifacts-123456789012-eu-west-1/9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08

items.title: !Rain::S3Http
items.text:
!Rain::S3Http <path> uploads the same way and inserts the HTTPS URL of the object:

Resources:
  Api:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Api
    Properties:
      StageName: prod
      DefinitionUri: !Rain::S3Http openapi.yaml

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Api:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Api
    Properties:
      StageName: prod
      DefinitionUri: https://rain-artifacts-123456789012-eu-west-1.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/a591a6d40bf420404a011733cfb7b190d62c65bf0bcda32b57b277d9ad9f146e

items.title: The object form
items.text:
Give !Rain::S3 a map instead of a path to control the upload and the output:

Resources:
  Function:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.main
      Role: !GetAtt FunctionRole.Arn
      Code: !Rain::S3
        Path: lambda-src
        Run: build.sh
        BucketProperty: S3Bucket
        KeyProperty: S3Key

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Function:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.main
      Role: !GetAtt FunctionRole.Arn
      Code:
        S3Bucket: rain-artifacts-123456789012-eu-west-1
        S3Key: 1b4844dacc843f09941c11c94f80981d3be8ae7578952c71e875ef7add37b1a7

items.title: Options
items.text: Option Value What it does Path A file or directory The content to upload. Required. Zip true or false Zip the path even when it is a single file. The default is false. A directory is always zipped. BucketProperty A property name With Format: Object, the name of the property that gets the bucket name KeyProperty A property name With Format: Object, the name of the property that gets the object key Format URI, Http or Object What to insert. See Format. Run A script path A script that cfnrain runs before the upload. See Run. Extension For example zip or sh Add .<Extension> to the object key

items.title: Format
items.text:
Format Output URI s3://<bucket>/<key> Http https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<key> Object A map with the bucket in BucketProperty and the key in KeyProperty

If you do not set Format, the default depends on the other options. When you set both BucketProperty and KeyProperty, the default is Object. Otherwise the default is URI.

The values are case sensitive. Write URI, not Uri. With Format: Uri, packaging stops with unexpected S3 output format: Uri. The cfnrain pkg help text, inherited from Rain, still shows Uri, which is wrong. See Known issues.

Format: Object without both property names stops with missing BucketProperty or KeyProperty.

items.title: Run
items.text:
Run names a script, relative to the template file. cfnrain runs it in the template's directory before the upload, with no arguments. Use it to build the content that Path points to:

#!/bin/sh
# build.sh
set -e
rm -rf lambda-src
mkdir lambda-src
cp src/*.py lambda-src/
pip install -r requirements.txt -t lambda-src

The script must be executable. If it fails, packaging stops. cfnrain shows the script output only with --debug.

Templates run code

Run executes a program from your computer when you package the template. Only package templates that you trust. This is not behind --experimental.

items.title: Extension
items.text:
Some services need a file extension on the object key. Extension adds it:

Resources:
  Document:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      DocumentType: Command
      Attachments:
        - Key: SourceUrl
          Values:
            - !Rain::S3
              Path: scripts/setup.sh
              Extension: sh

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Document:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      DocumentType: Command
      Attachments:
        - Key: SourceUrl
          Values:
            - s3://rain-artifacts-123456789012-eu-west-1/5891b5b522d5df086d0ff0b110fbd9d21bb4fc7163af34d08286a2e846f6be03.sh

items.title: Modules
items.text:
A module is a template file that another template includes. cfnrain inserts the module's resources into the parent template when it packages it. Modules let you split a large template into files and reuse a group of resources in many stacks.

Modules are a client-side feature. CloudFormation only sees the packaged template, so run cfnrain pkg to see the result. Run linters such as cfn-lint on the packaged template, because they do not know the Modules section.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The module, bucket-module.yaml:

Parameters:
  Name:
    Type: String

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Ref Name
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

Outputs:
  Arn:
    Value: !GetAtt Bucket.Arn

The parent template:

Modules:
  Logs:
    Source: ./bucket-module.yaml
    Properties:
      Name: billing-logs
    Overrides:
      Bucket:
        DeletionPolicy: Retain
        Properties:
          VersioningConfiguration:
            Status: Suspended

Outputs:
  LogsArn:
    Value: !GetAtt Logs.Arn

The packaged template:

Resources:
  LogsBucket:
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: billing-logs
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Suspended

Outputs:
  LogsArn:
    Value: !GetAtt LogsBucket.Arn

items.title: The Modules section
items.text:
Each entry in Modules has a name and a configuration:

Key What it does Source Where the module file is. See Sources. Properties Values for the module's Parameters Overrides Changes to the module's resources. See Overrides. ForEach Make one copy of the module for each item in a list. See ForEach.

items.title: Module files
items.text:
A module looks like a template. It can have Parameters, Resources, Conditions, Outputs, Constants, Modules and Packages. Any valid CloudFormation template works as a module.

The parent sets the module's parameters with Properties. A property can be a string, a list or an object. Inside the module, !Ref <Parameter> and ${Parameter} in a !Sub get the property value. If the parent does not set a property, cfnrain uses the parameter's Default.

items.title: Logical IDs
items.text: cfnrain adds the module name in front of each logical ID. The resource Bucket in the module Logs becomes LogsBucket. cfnrain also updates the Ref, GetAtt, Sub and DependsOn references inside the module.

items.title: Outputs
items.text:
The parent can use a module output with !GetAtt <Module>.<Output> or ${<Module>.<Output>} in a !Sub. cfnrain replaces the reference with the output value. In the example, !GetAtt Logs.Arn becomes !GetAtt LogsBucket.Arn.

You can also refer to a module resource by its new logical ID, such as !Ref LogsBucket. This works, but it breaks when the module author renames the resource. Outputs are safer.

items.title: Overrides
items.text:
Overrides changes the module's resources. The keys are the logical IDs inside the module. cfnrain merges the override into the resource:

  • A map merges with the map in the module, key by key.
  • A scalar replaces the value in the module.
  • A list adds its items to the list in the module. For example, an override can add a statement to a policy.
  • This works for Properties, Metadata, CreationPolicy and UpdatePolicy. You can also set DeletionPolicy, UpdateReplacePolicy and Condition, and add to DependsOn.

There is no way to remove a list item or a property with an override. An override must name a resource that exists in the module. It cannot set a property that has the same name as a module parameter. Set the parameter with Properties instead.

Overrides depend on the inside of the module. If the module changes, your overrides can break. Use parameters when the module offers them, and use overrides when it does not.

items.title: Sources
items.text:
Source can be:

  • A path relative to the file that has the Modules section, such as ./bucket-module.yaml or modules/vpc.yaml. It is not relative to the directory where you run cfnrain.
  • An https:// URL or an s3:// URI.
  • A path inside a package, such as $samples/encrypted-bucket.yaml. See Packages.

A module can include other modules. A module cannot include itself, directly or through other modules.

items.title: Conditions
items.text: cfnrain evaluates the module's conditions when it can. See IfParam and conditions.

items.title: Experimental status
items.text:
The Modules section does not need --experimental. Rain's old README said that it did, but the code does not check for it. Only the older !Rain::Module directive needs --experimental.

The feature is still young. The format can change in a minor release.

items.title: More tested examples
items.text:
The module tests in cft/pkg/tmpl/awscli-modules cover more cases. Each -template.yaml file has a matching -expect.yaml file with the packaged result. This one shows a module output in a !Sub, a GetAtt inside the module, and an override.

The module:

Parameters:
  Name:
    Type: String
Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Ref Name
      OverrideMe: abc
      SubName: !Sub ${Name}
  Bucket2:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !GetAtt Bucket.Something
Outputs:
  Name:
    Value: !Ref Bucket

The parent template:

Modules:
  Content:
    Source: ./basic-module.yaml
    Properties:
      Name: foo
    Overrides:
      Bucket:
        Properties:
          OverrideMe: def
Resources:
  OtherResource:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Metadata:
      TestOutputSub: !Sub ${Content.Name}

The packaged template:

Resources:
  OtherResource:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Metadata:
      TestOutputSub:
        Fn::Sub: ${ContentBucket}
  ContentBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: foo
      OverrideMe: def
      SubName: foo
  ContentBucket2:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName:
        Fn::GetAtt:
        - ContentBucket
        - Something

items.title: IfParam and conditions
items.text: A module can include or leave out resources based on the properties that the parent sets. There are two ways: the IfParam and IfNotParam metadata, and normal CloudFormation conditions.

items.title: IfParam and IfNotParam
items.text:
Add Metadata.Rain.IfParam or Metadata.Rain.IfNotParam to a resource in a module:

  • IfParam: <Parameter> keeps the resource only when the parent sets that property.
  • IfNotParam: <Parameter> keeps the resource only when the parent does not set that property.

cfnrain removes the IfParam and IfNotParam keys from the output. IfParam only works in modules.

Use IfParam for optional parts of a module, such as permissions for a resource that the parent passes in. Use IfNotParam when the parent can bring its own resource instead of the one that the module creates.

The module, queue-module.yaml:

Parameters:
  DeadLetterArn:
    Type: String

Resources:
  Queue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Metadata:
      Rain:
        IfParam: DeadLetterArn
    Properties:
      RedrivePolicy:
        deadLetterTargetArn: !Ref DeadLetterArn
        maxReceiveCount: 5
  SimpleQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Metadata:
      Rain:
        IfNotParam: DeadLetterArn

The parent template:

Modules:
  Orders:
    Source: ./queue-module.yaml
    Properties:
      DeadLetterArn: arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:orders-dlq
  Events:
    Source: ./queue-module.yaml

The packaged template:

Resources:
  OrdersQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      RedrivePolicy:
        deadLetterTargetArn: arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:orders-dlq
        maxReceiveCount: 5

  EventsSimpleQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue

Orders sets DeadLetterArn, so it gets Queue with a redrive policy. Events does not, so it gets SimpleQueue.

items.title: Conditions in modules
items.text:
A module can have a Conditions section. cfnrain evaluates each condition when it packages the template:

  • If the condition resolves to false, cfnrain removes the resources, modules and outputs that use it, and picks the false branch of each Fn::If.
  • If the condition resolves to true, cfnrain keeps them and picks the true branch.
  • cfnrain removes values that are !Ref AWS::NoValue.
  • If cfnrain cannot resolve the condition, for example because it uses AWS::Region or a parameter of the parent template, it copies the condition to the parent template. The condition name gets the module name in front, like a logical ID.

items.title: Resolved conditions
items.text:
The module:

Parameters:
  Foo:
    Type: String

Conditions:
  Show0:
    Fn::Equals:
      - !Ref Foo
      - bar
  Show1:
    Fn::And:
      - Fn::Equals:
        - !Ref Foo
        - bar
      - Condition: Show0
  Show2:
    Fn::Not:
    - Fn::Or:
        - Fn::Equals:
          - !Ref Foo
          - baz
        - Fn::Equals:
          - Fn::If:
            - Fn::Equals:
              - a
              - a
            - x
            - y
          - y

Resources:
  Bucket0:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: Show0
  Bucket1:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: Show1
  Bucket2:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: Show2

The parent template:

Modules:
  A:
    Source: ./cond-intrinsics-module.yaml
    Properties:
      Foo: bar
  B:
    Source: ./cond-intrinsics-module.yaml
    Properties:
      Foo: baz

The packaged template. Module A has Foo: bar, so every condition is true. Module B has Foo: baz, so every condition is false and none of its buckets are in the output.

Resources:
  ABucket0:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
  ABucket1:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
  ABucket2:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket

items.title: Unresolved conditions
items.text:
The parent template:

Parameters:
  P:
    Type: String

Modules:
  Foo:
    Source: cond-unres-module.yaml
    Properties:
      P: !Ref P

The module, cond-unres-module.yaml:

Parameters:
  P:
    Type: String

Conditions:
  IsRegionUsEast1:
    Fn::Equals:
    - Ref: AWS::Region
    - us-east-1
  IsPTrue:
    Fn::Equals:
      - !Ref P
      - true

Modules:
  Sub:
    Source: cond-unres-submodule.yaml
    Properties:
      P: !Ref P

Resources:
  S3Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: IsRegionUsEast1
  A:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name:
        Fn::If:
          - IsRegionUsEast1
          - a-east
          - a-not-east
  C:
    Type: D::E::F
    Condition: IsPTrue

The submodule, cond-unres-submodule.yaml:

Parameters:
