  P:
    Type: String

Conditions:
  IsParam:
    Fn::Equals:
      - !Ref P
      - true

Resources:
  B:
    Condition: IsParam
    Type: A::B::C

The packaged template. The conditions depend on the region and on the parent parameter P, so they move to the parent with the prefixes Foo and FooSub.

Parameters:
  P:
    Type: String
Conditions:
  FooIsRegionUsEast1:
    Fn::Equals:
    - Ref: AWS::Region
    - us-east-1
  FooIsPTrue:
    Fn::Equals:
      - !Ref P
      - true
  FooSubIsParam:
    Fn::Equals:
      - !Ref P
      - true

Resources:
  FooS3Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: FooIsRegionUsEast1
  FooA:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name:
        Fn::If:
          - FooIsRegionUsEast1
          - a-east
          - a-not-east
  FooSubB:
    Type: A::B::C
    Condition: FooSubIsParam
  FooC:
    Type: D::E::F
    Condition: FooIsPTrue

items.title: Constants section
items.text:
A template or a module can have a top-level Constants: section. A constant is a string or an object that you write once and use in many places. cfnrain replaces the constants and removes the section when it packages the template.

Constants:
  S3Arn: "arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::"
  BucketName: "${Name}-${AWS::Region}-${AWS::AccountId}"
  BucketArn: "${Const::S3Arn}${Const::BucketName}"
  Tags:
    Team: platform

Use a constant in two ways:

  • ${Const::<Name>} inside a !Sub string inserts a string constant.
  • !Ref Const::<Name> inserts an object constant. You can only insert the whole object, not a part of it.

A constant can use the constants above it with ${Const::<Name>}. cfnrain replaces the constants before it processes the modules. If a !Sub has no variables left after that, cfnrain replaces it with a plain string.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The parent template:

Constants:
  yyy: zzz
Metadata:
  test: !Sub ${Const::yyy}
Modules:
  Content:
    Source: ./constant-module.yaml

The module, constant-module.yaml:

Constants:
  foo: bar
  sub: "${Const::foo}-abc-${AWS::AccountId}"
  obj:
    TestObject:
      A: b

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Metadata:
      Test: !Sub ${Const::sub}-xyz
      TestObj: !Ref Const::obj
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub ${Const::foo}

The packaged template:

Metadata:
  test: zzz
Resources:
  ContentBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Metadata:
      Test:
        Fn::Sub: bar-abc-${AWS::AccountId}-xyz
      TestObj:
        TestObject:
          A: b
    Properties:
      BucketName: bar

The parent's ${Const::yyy} becomes the plain string zzz. In the module, ${Const::sub} keeps ${AWS::AccountId}, so it stays a Fn::Sub.

items.title: Two constant systems
items.text:
cfnrain has two ways to write constants. Both work.

Constants: section Rain: section Where Top level of a template or module Rain: Constants: In a !Sub ${Const::Name} ${Rain::Name} Insert a value !Ref Const::Name !Rain::Constant Name Page This page Constants and !Rain::Constant

cfnrain replaces both ${Rain::Name} and ${Const::Name} in !Sub strings. Pick one system per template, so readers know where to look.

items.title: ForEach
items.text:
ForEach makes one copy of a module for each item in a list. There are two forms: the ForEach key on a module, and Fn::ForEach in the Modules section.

The list must be known when cfnrain packages the template. It can be a comma-separated string, or !Ref to a CommaDelimitedList parameter with a Default. cfnrain uses the default value. It cannot use a value that CloudFormation resolves at deploy time.

items.title: The ForEach key
items.text:
Add ForEach to a module entry. In the module's Properties, two placeholders are available:

Placeholder Value $Identifier The current list item $Index The position of the item in the list, from 0

There is no $MapValue placeholder. An old example in the Rain README used it, but the code never supported it.

cfnrain adds the index to the module name: Data0, Data1, Data2. So the resource Bucket becomes Data0Bucket, Data1Bucket and Data2Bucket.

The module, bucket-module.yaml:

Parameters:
  Name:
    Type: String

Resources:
  Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Ref Name
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

Outputs:
  Arn:
    Value: !GetAtt Bucket.Arn

The parent template:

Parameters:
  Envs:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Default: dev,stage,prod

Modules:
  Data:
    Source: ./bucket-module.yaml
    ForEach: !Ref Envs
    Properties:
      Name: billing-$Identifier-$Index

Outputs:
  ProdArn:
    Value: !GetAtt Data[2].Arn
  AllArns:
    Value: !Join
      - ","
      - !GetAtt Data[].Arn

The packaged template:

Parameters:
  Envs:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Default: dev,stage,prod

Resources:
  Data0Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: billing-dev-0
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

  Data1Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: billing-stage-1
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

  Data2Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: billing-prod-2
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled

Outputs:
  ProdArn:
    Value: !GetAtt Data2Bucket.Arn

  AllArns:
    Value: !Join
      - ','
      - - !GetAtt Data0Bucket.Arn
        - !GetAtt Data1Bucket.Arn
        - !GetAtt Data2Bucket.Arn

items.title: Outputs of a loop
items.text:
Reference Result !GetAtt Data[2].Arn The output of one copy, by index !GetAtt Data[prod].Arn The output of one copy, by list item !GetAtt Data[].Arn A list with the output of every copy ${Data[0].Arn} in a !Sub The output of one copy, in a string

In another module with the same ForEach list, !GetAtt Data[$Index].Arn refers to the copy with the same index.

items.title: Fn::ForEach
items.text:
Fn::ForEach::<LoopName> in the Modules section uses the syntax of the CloudFormation AWS::LanguageExtensions transform. It takes three items: an identifier name, the list, and a map from a module name to a module configuration. Use the identifier as ${Name} in the properties, or &{Name} in the module name.

If the identifier is in the module name, the copies use the list item in their names, such as BBFoo. If it is not, cfnrain adds the index, such as A0Foo.

The module:

Parameters:
  Name:
    Type: String
Resources:
  Foo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref Name
Outputs:
  Out1:
    Value: !GetAtt Foo.Arn

The parent template:

Modules:
  Fn::ForEach::A:
    - TheKey
    - A,B,C
    - A:
        Source: foreach-module.yaml
        Properties:
          Name: a-${TheKey}
  Fn::ForEach::B:
    - TheKey
    - A,B,C
    - B&{TheKey}:
        Source: foreach-module.yaml
        Properties:
          Name: b-${TheKey}
Outputs:
  TestGetAttA:
    Value: !GetAtt A[0].Out1
  TestGetAttB:
    Value: !GetAtt B[B].Out1

The packaged template:

Resources:
  A0Foo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name: a-A
  A1Foo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name: a-B
  A2Foo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name: a-C
  BAFoo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name: b-A
  BBFoo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name: b-B
  BCFoo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Name: b-C
Outputs:
  TestGetAttA:
    Value: !GetAtt A0Foo.Arn
  TestGetAttB:
    Value: !GetAtt BBFoo.Arn

Fn::ForEach outside the Modules section is not processed by cfnrain. CloudFormation processes it if the template uses the AWS::LanguageExtensions transform.

items.title: Intrinsic functions
items.text:
cfnrain adds some intrinsic functions that CloudFormation does not have. cfnrain resolves them when it packages the template, so CloudFormation never sees them. It also simplifies Fn::Join and Fn::Select when it can.

Function Short form Where it works Fn::Merge !Merge In module resources Fn::InsertFile !InsertFile Anywhere Fn::Invoke !Invoke In a template that has a Modules section

Fn::Merge only runs in modules

In the resources of the parent template, cfnrain leaves Fn::Merge as it is. CloudFormation has no Fn::Merge, so a deploy with Fn::Merge outside a module fails.

items.title: Fn::Merge
items.text:
Fn::Merge merges a list of maps into one map, or a list of lists into one list. For maps, a later key replaces an earlier one. For lists, cfnrain joins the lists and keeps duplicates.

Use it to combine values that come from module properties, such as tags from the parent and tags from the module.

The module:

Parameters:
  X:
    Type: Object
  Y:
    Type: Object
  XX:
    Type: List
  YY:
    Type: List
Resources:
  Bar:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Merged:
        Fn::Merge:
        - !Ref X
        - !Ref Y
      Lists:
        Fn::Merge:
        - !Ref XX
        - !Ref YY
        - !Ref YY

The parent template:

Modules:
  Foo:
    Source: merge-module.yaml
    Properties:
      X: 
        A: "BBB"
        B: "c"
      Y:
        B: "CCC"
        C: "D"
      XX:
      - a
      - b
      YY:
      - b
      - c

The packaged template:

Resources:
  FooBar:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Merged:
        A: BBB
        B: CCC
        C: D
      Lists:
      - a
      - b
      - b
      - c
      - b
      - c

items.title: Fn::InsertFile
items.text:
Fn::InsertFile <path> inserts the contents of a file as a string. The path is relative to the template. Unlike !Rain::Embed, it keeps the whitespace at the end of the file.

The template:

Resources:
  Foo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Content:
        Fn::InsertFile: insertfile-file.yaml

insertfile-file.yaml:

Test: abc

The packaged template:

Resources:
  Foo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Content: 'Test: abc

        '

items.title: Fn::Invoke
items.text:
Fn::Invoke calls a module like a function. It takes three items:

  1. The name of a module in the Modules section
  2. A map of properties. These replace the properties that the Modules section sets.
  3. The name of a module output

cfnrain evaluates the module with the new properties and inserts the output. A module for Invoke does not need resources. Parameters and Outputs are enough. A common use is a naming module that joins an environment, an application and a resource name.

The naming module, invoke-module.yaml:

Description: This module outputs a consistent resource name

Parameters:

  Env:
    Type: String
    Description: The environment, for example, dev, stage, prod

  App:
    Type: String
    Description: The application name

  Name:
    Type: String
    Description: The name of the resource

  Delimiter:
    Type: String
    Default: "-"

  MaxLength:
    Type: Integer
    Description: If the components exceed this, truncate and append a hash

  IncludeRegion:
    Type: Boolean
    Default: false

  IncludeAccount:
    Type: Boolean
    Default: false

  LabelOrder:
    Type: List<String>
    Default:
      - Name
      - App
      - Env
      - Region
      - Account

Conditions:

  IncludeRegion:
    Fn::Equals:
      - !Ref IncludeRegion
      - true

Resources:

  Why:
    Type: X::Y::Z
    Properties:
      Id:  
        Fn::Join:
          - !Ref Delimiter
          - - !Ref Name
            - !Ref App
            - !Ref Env
            - Fn::If:
              - IncludeRegion
              - !Ref AWS::Region
              - !Ref AWS::NoValue

Outputs:

  Id:
    Value:
      Fn::Join:
        - !Ref Delimiter
        - - !Ref Name
          - !Ref App
          - !Ref Env
          - Fn::If:
            - IncludeRegion
            - !Ref AWS::Region
            - !Ref AWS::NoValue

A module that returns an object, invoke-module-b.yaml:

Parameters:
  X:
    Type: String
  Y: 
    Type: String
  Z:
    Type: String

Outputs:
  Props:
    Value:
      X: !Ref X
      Y: !Ref Y
      Z: !Ref Z

The parent template:

Modules:

  Label:
    Source: invoke-module.yaml
    Properties:
      Env: prod
      App: myapp
      Name: "?"

  HIJProps:
    Source: invoke-module-b.yaml
    Properties:
      X: x
      Y: y
      Z: z


Resources:

  A:
    Type: D::E::F
    Properties:
      Name: 
        Fn::Invoke:
          - Label
          - Name: test
          - Id
      Name2: !Invoke [Label, {Name: test2}, Id]
      WithRegion: !Invoke [Label, {Name: test3, IncludeRegion: true}, Id]

  B: 
    Type: H::I::J
    Properties: 
      Fn::Invoke:
        - HIJProps
        - Y: yy
        - Props

  C:
    Type: H::I::J
    Properties: !Invoke [HIJProps, {Z: zz}, Props]

The packaged template:

Resources:
  A:
    Type: D::E::F
    Properties:
      Name: test-myapp-prod
      Name2: test2-myapp-prod
      WithRegion:
        Fn::Join:
        - '-'
        - - test3
          - myapp
          - prod
          - Ref: AWS::Region
  B:
    Type: H::I::J
    Properties:
      X: x
      Y: yy
      Z: z
  C:
    Type: H::I::J
    Properties:
      X: x
      Y: y
      Z: zz
  LabelWhy:
    Type: X::Y::Z
    Properties:
      Id: ?-myapp-prod

The Label module also has a resource, Why. cfnrain adds it to the template as LabelWhy, with the properties from the Modules section. Fn::Invoke does not add resources.

items.title: Fn::Join and Fn::Select
items.text:
cfnrain also simplifies two CloudFormation functions when it can resolve them while it packages the template:

  • Fn::Join becomes a plain string when every item in the list is a string. This works in the parent template and in modules.
  • Fn::Select becomes the selected item when the list and the index are known.

Fn::Select takes its arguments in the reverse order

cfnrain simplifies Fn::Select only when the list comes first and the index second: Fn::Select: [!Ref Things, 0]. CloudFormation uses the opposite order: Fn::Select: [0, !Ref Things]. If you use the CloudFormation order, cfnrain leaves the function as it is and CloudFormation resolves it. That works. If you use the cfnrain order and cfnrain cannot resolve the list, CloudFormation gets the arguments in the wrong order and the deploy fails. Use the CloudFormation order. See Known issues.

The test for Fn::Select uses the cfnrain order:

Parameters:
  Things:
    Type: List<String>
Resources:
  Foo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Names: !Ref Things
      OneName: 
        Fn::Select:
        - !Ref Things
        - 0

Modules:
  TestSelect:
    Source: select-module.yaml
    Properties:
      Things:
      - foo
      - bar

The packaged template:

Resources:
  TestSelectFoo:
    Type: A::B::C
    Properties:
      Names:
      - foo
      - bar
      OneName: foo

items.title: Packages
items.text: A package is a zip file with modules in it. The Packages section gives a package a short alias. A module Source that starts with $<alias>/ refers to a file inside that package.

items.title: The Packages section
items.text:
Packages:
  samples:
    Source: https://github.com/awesome-foundation/cfnrain/releases/download/v1.25.2/modules.zip
    Hash: https://github.com/awesome-foundation/cfnrain/releases/download/v1.25.2/modules.sha256

Modules:
  Data:
    Source: $samples/encrypted-bucket.yaml
Key What it does Source The zip file: a local path, an https:// URL or an s3:// URI Hash Optional. A URL or a local path to a file that has the SHA-256 hash of the zip, as hex. If the hash does not match, packaging stops with hash does not match.

A local zip works the same way. This test packages a module from package.zip:

The template:

Packages:
  abc: 
    Source: package.zip

Modules:
  Test:
    Source: $abc/zip-module.yaml

zip-module.yaml, inside package.zip:

Resources:
  Test:
    Type: A::B::C

The packaged template:

Resources:
  TestTest:
    Type: A::B::C

items.title: Sample modules
items.text:
Each cfnrain release has modules.zip and modules.sha256, with the sample modules from the modules directory. Use them as examples for your own modules:

Module What it creates simple-vpc.yaml A VPC with two availability zones encrypted-bucket.yaml A bucket with encryption and blocked public access compliant-bucket.yaml A bucket with log and replica buckets and a bucket policy, made to pass common compliance checks bucket-policy.yaml A bucket policy that denies requests without TLS load-balancer.yaml An Elastic Load Balancing v2 load balancer static-site.yaml An S3 bucket and a CloudFront distribution for a static web site cognito.yaml A Cognito user pool and related resources rest-api.yaml An API Gateway REST API api-resource.yaml A Lambda function and its API Gateway resources simple-table.yaml A DynamoDB table

items.title: Packages in the Rain section
items.text:
The Rain: section can also define packages, with Location instead of Source. This is the older form. It works with a resource Type that starts with $<alias>/. cfnrain turns that type into the older !Rain::Module directive, so it needs --experimental.

Rain:
  Packages:
    abc:
      Location: ./my-modules
Resources:
  Foo:
    Type: $abc/bucket.yaml

items.title: The older !Rain::Module directive
items.text:
Before the Modules section, Rain had module resources: a resource with Type: !Rain::Module <uri>. They still work, for compatibility, and need --experimental:

Resources:
  Show1Hide2:
    Type: !Rain::Module ./ifparam-module.yaml
    Properties:
      Foo: foo

Without --experimental, packaging stops with You must add the --experimental arg to use the !Rain::Module directive. Use the Modules section for new templates.

The pkg help text in Rain said that a !Rain::Module file must have a resource called ModuleExtension with Metadata.Extends. The code does not check for either of these.

items.title: CodeArtifact modules (experimental)
items.text:
cfnrain module publishes a directory of module files to AWS CodeArtifact as a generic package, and installs it again. Every module command needs -x (--experimental).

# Create the CodeArtifact domain and repository
cfnrain module bootstrap -x

# Publish the modules in ./modules as version 1.0.0
cfnrain module publish -x my-modules --path modules --version 1.0.0

# Install them into ./vendor/my-modules
cfnrain module install -x my-modules --path vendor/my-modules --version 1.0.0
Flag Default What it does --domain cloudformation The CodeArtifact domain --repo rain The CodeArtifact repository --path . The local directory to publish from, or to install to --version The package version. install uses the latest version when you do not set it.

install checks the SHA-256 hash of the package against CodeArtifact before it unzips it. After the install, refer to the modules with a local Source path.
